name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: DO: Replace the current prompt-review system with a shared log that records every prompt sent, its engine, routing rule, and timestamp. This makes changes auditable and lets us spot regressions or drift in real time. The trade-off is storage cost and slight latency from logging—but the clarity it gives outweighs that.

name: Gauge
text: Sprocket’s shared log buries decisions under noise—no discipline, no rollback, no way to prove a regression was a one-off. A better alternative: a minimal, versioned changelog that ties each prompt change to a decision record and a rollback point. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot: if the log doesn’t cut mean-time-to-recovery for prompt regressions, scrap it.
